page: Hetzner Cloud cx23 is an entry-level virtual server within the Cost Optimized family, running on the QEMU hypervisor. It is configured with 2 shared vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, 4.0 GB of system memory (1.95 GB per core), and a bundled 40 GB NVMe SSD local drive. The instance does not include a dedicated GPU (0.0 count) or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Hardware instruction support covers AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and standard bit-manipulation extensions, while advanced acceleration sets such as AMX or AVX-512 VNNI are not present.

Benchmark measurements position the cx23 in the lower tiers of raw processing and throughput. Synthetic compute assessments yield a Geekbench single-core score of 713.0, a multi-core score of 1233.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 2394.06. Memory performance registers an uncached read bandwidth of 20.91 GB/sec and an uncached write bandwidth of 16.93 GB/sec. Across operational workloads, the server handles 2.52 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves 1.77 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given the shared vCPU design and modest compute output, the cx23 prioritizes baseline resource efficiency over sustained heavy computation. The inclusion of high-speed NVMe storage provides responsive local I/O, though the total memory footprint and shared CPU allocation constrain scalability. These characteristics make the instance suitable for lightweight web serving, development environments, small-scale utility microservices, and modest background task processing.
